What the Government is doing

What was decided or announced, who said it, and where it goes next. Every point carries the words it was taken from.

Motion on Singapore's economic future, amended and agreed to

Motion as amended agreed to5 August 2026 motion-3008, motion-3010

A Motion moved by Mr Kenneth Tiong and seconded by Assoc Prof Jamus Lim, proposing principles for a more equal and inclusive economy and an economic engine driven by local companies, domestic demand and Singaporeans venturing abroad, which was debated and amended.

The amended Motion records the House's belief in a more equal and inclusive economy and an economy powered by dynamic local companies, global enterprises, healthy domestic and external demand, and Singaporeans and Singaporean capital venturing abroad. The transcript does not state any direct change to law or schemes from the Motion itself. The record does not set out the practical impact.

Open questions from this debate (9)

Questions the debate raises that the record does not resolve. Listed as open questions, not as findings.

  • Whether mandatory retrenchment benefits will be legislated, and what impact that would have on employers, SMEs and hiring.
  • How many Enterprise Singapore-supported SMEs that applied for internationalisation programmes succeeded and remained in foreign markets after five years, and what the internal rate of return for those grants is.
  • Whether the Government will adopt the proposed NTU special zone, the new land use category for restricted tenure, non-tradable, mixed housing and enterprise land, or the proposed zone authority.
  • Whether the Government will cap annual rent increases for SMEs or revisit dependency ratio ceilings for sectors such as F&B.
  • What specific macroeconomic targets beyond top-line growth the Government will commit to, and whether a consolidated report card for the four economic blueprints will be published.
  • Whether the Government will set a target for Singapore-headquartered companies with more than $1 billion in revenue.
  • How the proposed shared use of research labs and equipment would be managed.
  • Whether the Government will expand funding lines for early-stage high-failure, high-impact deep tech ventures as proposed.
  • What the practical impact of the amended Motion will be for ordinary Singaporeans.
